title: The impact of prophylactic azithromycin on the developing preterm gut microbiome and resistome.
authors: Ahearn-Ford S, Aboklaish A, Young GR, Lowe J, Masi AC, Gallacher D, Marchesi JR, Berrington JE
abstract: Early-life antibiotic exposure can profoundly impact the developing preterm gut microbiome and resistome, with short- and long-term consequences for health. In a large multi-center (n = 28) study of 693 preterm infants, we investigated the effects of 10 d of prophylactic intravenous azithromycin on the gut microbiome and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). The AZithromycin ThErapy for Chronic Lung Disease of Prematurity (AZTEC) study was a double blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of preterm infants (born < 30 weeks of gestation), treated from birth for 10 d with either intravenous azithromycin or placebo, and sampled longitudinally for 21 d or discharge. Using 16S rRNA gene sequencing, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and quantitative PCR, we show azithromycin reduced microbial diversity and the relative abundance of health-associated Bifidobacterium and increased relative abundances of pathobionts Staphylococcus and Enterobacter/Klebsiella. This early azithromycin treatment increased the number of macrolide-resistant genes, including the presence of erm (C), which persisted for the duration of the study. Probiotic use (at individual unit discretion) increased alpha diversity and Bifidobacterium relative abundance, but did not fully mitigate the effects of azithromycin receipt. Combined azithromycin and probiotics further increased the enrichment of Enterobacter/Klebsiella and total ARGs, including erm(C). These findings highlight the impacts of antibiotic and probiotic use, both important in balancing infection control issues and microbiome disruption and antimicrobial resistance.
publication_types: Journal Article, Randomized Controlled Trial, Multicenter Study

title: Advanced cell-instructive bio-inks: Engineering multiscale niches for functional tissue formation.
authors: Ng WL, Xu Y, Liu F, Bartolo P
abstract: Three-dimensional bioprinting has transformed tissue fabrication by enabling the precise spatial organization of living cells and biomaterials into biomimetic tissue constructs. However, advances in manufacturing have outpaced the development of bio-inks capable of actively directing tissue formation. Most existing bio-inks remain optimized for printability, rheological behaviour, and structural fidelity, while providing limited control over the biological processes that govern tissue morphogenesis, functional maturation, and regeneration. This review examines the emerging paradigm of cell-instructive bio-inks, which integrate biological regulation directly into material design to recreate the cellular microenvironments that guide tissue development. We present a unifying framework that classifies these bio-inks according to three complementary regulatory dimensions: biochemical niches that regulate cell fate through molecular signalling and regenerative matrices; architectural niches that direct tissue organization through spatial and structural cues; and metabolic niches that modulate oxygen availability, redox homeostasis, and cellular metabolism. We further discuss strategies for integrating these instructive functions within multifunctional bio-inks, together with scalable manufacturing, and artificial intelligence-assisted bio-ink design. By redefining bio-inks as active regulators of cellular behaviour, this review establishes a conceptual framework for engineering next-generation bio-inks capable of orchestrating tissue development, functional maturation, and regenerative outcomes.

title: The application progress of detection technology for Bacillus cereus in food: Challenges, innovations and future prospects.
authors: Zhang Y, Zhang X, Zheng H, Wang H, Yu M, Jia W, Jia Z, Cui J
abstract: Food safety is a key issue of global public health. As a foodborne pathogen - Bacillus cereus (B. cereus), it is widely distributed in nature and can cause diseases in both humans and animals. The rapid detection of B. cereus is of great significance for the prevention and control of such diseases. This article provides a detailed overview of the development of B. cereus detection techniques in food, transitioning from traditional methods to a series of current technologies such as immunology, molecular biology and MALDI-TOF-MS. The principles, advantages and disadvantages of various detection techniques, as well as their application progress, were outlined. Furthermore, the application and advantages of combining different techniques in the detection of B. cereus in food were demonstrated. The CRISPR/Cas system possesses the characteristics of high specificity, high sensitivity and ease of operation, and shows great potential in the field of foodborne pathogen detection. This article also explains that the combination of CRISPR/Cas technology with RPA, LFA and AI technologies can further enhance the detection rate and accuracy. The aforementioned technology can enable the early detection and prevention of B. cereus in food, ensuring food safety and preventing the outbreak of foodborne diseases. This article has certain reference value in the research on the detection techniques of B. cereus and other foodborne pathogens in food, and provides strong support for safeguarding food safety and maintaining human health.

title: Advances and perspectives in genetically encoded biosensors for biomarker detection and theranostic circuits.
authors: Xu J, Qi Q, Wang Q
abstract: Effective biomarker detection is critical for timely and accurate clinical disease diagnosis. However, conventional analytical methodologies are often constrained by laborious procedures, reliance on specialized equipment, and an inherent inability to perform continuous in situ monitoring. To circumvent these limitations, synthetic biology has pioneered the development of genetically encoded biosensors as a rapid, highly sensitive, and cost-effective alternative. This review specifically focuses on transcriptional regulation-based biosensors, primarily those utilizing allosteric transcription factors (aTFs) and two-component systems (TCSs). By integrating these regulatory sensing modules into engineered microbial chassis, researchers can achieve continuous, real-time biomarker monitoring even within complex and otherwise inaccessible physiological environments. This review particularly focuses on microbial chassis rather than mammalian systems due to their highly tractable genetics, rapid response kinetics, and their unique potential to be deployed as autonomous living probiotics for in situ theranostics. Furthermore, coupling these sensors with engineered actuator genes enables the construction of intelligent therapeutic genetic circuits. This closed-loop theranostic paradigm facilitates simultaneous, real-time diagnosis and autonomous, localized therapeutic interventions, paving the way for personalized and dose-adaptive precision medicine. Finally, we summarize recent advancements in these biosensor platforms, explore their applications in targeted disease interventions, and discuss the contemporary challenges alongside future perspectives for their clinical translation.

title: Transposable elements as dual agents in livestock-parasite interactions: From parasite adaptation to host genetic innovation.
authors: Omara A, Moawad AS, Ge J, Geng T
abstract: Transposable elements (TEs), which were previously seen as genomic parasites, are currently viewed as major contributors to evolutionary innovation in host-parasite interactions. This review provides an overview of the current knowledge of TEs in veterinary parasitology, divided into three interlinked levels. Firstly, in terms of parasite genome biology, TEs are highly diverse and actively transposing, from the extremely active mobilomes of strongylid nematodes and liver flukes to the TE-rich but genomically reduced microsporidian parasites. Secondly, at the host-parasite interface, direct physical contacts help in the horizontal exchange of TEs between the parasites and their hosts. Thirdly, TE activity leads to important functional innovations, including expansions of virulence-related gene families in schistosomes, formation of species-specific stage-regulated non-coding RNAs in liver flukes, and even TE-derived small interfering RNAs secreted by parasitic nematodes as cross-species immune modulators. On the host side, polymorphic TEs, especially SINEs and endogenous retroviruses, provide abundant opportunities to generate phenotypic diversity in livestock by affecting features such as muscle formation, fat accumulation, fur coloration, and immune response. Throughout this review, we clearly separate the established facts from the associations and hypotheses, and highlight the areas of knowledge deficit. In conclusion, we will outline the model of utilizing TE biomarkers in selective breeding, and note that the association between particular polymorphisms of TEs and resistance to parasites is mostly hypothetical and needs further verification.

title: When the earth shakes on fragile foundations: the Venezuelan earthquakes and two decades of public health system erosion.
authors: Paníz-Mondolfi AE, Chaccour C, Carrión-Nessi FS, Acosta-Serrano Á, Zambrano O, Gabaldón-Figueira JC, Grillet ME
abstract: The two earthquakes that recently struck the northern coast of Venezuela will deepen a health crisis that has troubled the country for twenty years. They have exposed how weak its health infrastructure is, how scarce medicines are, how little epidemiological surveillance remains, and how long investment has been lacking. The humanitarian health crisis in Venezuela did not arise from armed conflict, as it has elsewhere. Its roots lie in decades of authoritarian rule and institutional decay, which have eroded public health capacity, research infrastructure, vaccination coverage and the control of infectious diseases in general. Because these weaknesses have accumulated, the earthquakes may well turn into an even graver humanitarian emergency. Recovery that lasts will not be secured by short-term international aid alone. It will require the rebuilding of accountable institutions able to govern transparently and to apply equitable health policies, so that the health system can regain its resilience.

title: Strategy for enhanced production of A40926B0 in Nonomuraea gerenzanensis using an efficient CRISPR/AsCas12f1 system.
authors: Wang X, Zhai H, Gu D, Wang Y, Gao J, Du L, Zhuo L, Li X
abstract: The global emergence of vancomycin-resistant Gram-positive pathogens underscores the urgent need for efficient production of novel lipoglycopeptide antibiotics. Dalbavancin, a last-resort therapeutic agent, relies on its key biosynthetic precursor A40926B0, whose industrial manufacture is severely limited by the low yield of wild-type Nonomuraea gerenzanensis and inefficient genetic tools for this rare actinomycete. Here, we developed a high-efficiency CRISPR/AsCas12f1 genome editing system and applied systematic metabolic engineering to boost A40926B0 biosynthesis. First, conjugation conditions were optimized to elevate the transfer efficiency in N. gerenzanensis D11. The hypercompact AsCas12f1 nuclease showed markedly lower cytotoxicity than SpCas9 and enabled 100% gene deletion efficiency with preferred PAMs (TTTG, CTTG, GTTG). Second, we strengthened the shikimate pathway via multiple genetic strategies: overexpressing feedback-resistant DAHP synthase (aroG fbr ) and chorismate mutase/prephenate dehydrogenase (tyrA fbr ), as well as knocking out pheA. This manipulation blocks the phenylalanine synthetic branch and redirects metabolic flux toward the l-tyrosine branch. Third, we engineered the branched-chain fatty acid (BCFA) pathway via promoter replacement of bkdA2B2C2, LipAB, fabF and deletion of acdH to enhance isododecanoyl side-chain supply. The combinatorial engineering yielded strain B-13, which produced 1740 mg/L A40926B0 in shake flasks. Finally, 50-L fed-batch fermentation with continuous maltodextrin feeding further increased the titer to 1817 mg/L, the highest reported titer to date. This work establishes a robust CRISPR editing tool for N. gerenzanensis and provides valuable engineering references for precursor-oriented strain improvement targeting lipoglycopeptide antibiotics, offering insights for the industrial scale production of A40926B0.

title: Unsupervised high-resolution 3D MRI motion correction via physics-informed implicit neural representations.
authors: Le H, Wu Q, Li B, Zhang Y, Wei H
abstract: Motion-corrupted inverse problems remain a central bottleneck in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), especially for high-resolution 3D acquisitions where long readouts couple rigid-body displacement with non-Cartesian k-space sampling. We present a physics-informed implicit neural representation (INR) that recasts 3D motion correction as continuous neural field estimation. The method embeds a differentiable rigid-body motion operator into the INR forward model, enabling joint, zero-shot optimization of the motion trajectory and motion-free volume directly from raw k-space, without external navigators or paired supervision. By enforcing strict data consistency in a coordinate-based representation, the framework yields globally coherent reconstructions and mitigates hallucination risks under severe motion. Across simulated perturbations and real in-vivo high-resolution radial scans, our approach consistently improves motion estimation accuracy, structural preservation, downstream segmentation, and generalizes across subjects and protocols. Remarkably, for kooshball acquisitions with motion severity up to 10°/20mm, our method outperforms the navigator-based method by approximately 2 dB in peak signal-to-noise ratio. These results establish a unified paradigm for unsupervised, physics-consistent artificial intelligence solving of motion-corrupted MRI inverse problems, with broad applicability beyond a single sequence or anatomy. The source code is available at: https://github.com/AMRI-Lab/MoCo-3DRadial.

title: Systematic evaluation of the DNA repair machinery facilitated the development of efficient genome editing tools for the red yeast Rhodotorula toruloides.
authors: Chen Q, Lyu L, Wang S, Zhao ZK
abstract: The red yeast Rhodotorula toruloides is a robust lipid producer, and its biotechnology applications have been expanded through genetic engineering based on the non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) pathway. As the NHEJ pathway leads to random integration, it remains laborious in phenotypic assessment and challenging for rational strain design. To develop more efficient genetic tools for R. toruloides based on the homologous recombination (HR) pathway, we conducted a systematic evaluation of its DNA repair machinery. Overexpression of HR-related proteins, such as ScRad52, RtRad54 and ScSae2, increased the HR efficiency from less than 0.1% to 3.6%. In addition, knockout of RtKU70 and RtKU80 elevated the HR efficiency to 4.2% and 5.3%, respectively, but reduced resistance to mutagenic stress. Accordingly, we combined the two aforementioned strategies, which yielded an HR efficiency of 5.9%. Although this combined strategy failed to further elevate HR efficiency as expected, it partially alleviated the hypersensitivity to mutagenic stress caused by Ku protein inactivation. Remarkably, when the CRISPR-Cas9 system was used to introduce double-strand breaks (DSBs), HR efficiency was dramatically increased to 16%, and further overexpression of ScRAD52 led to higher HR efficiency of 75-95% across multiple genomic loci. These results will facilitate advanced genetic engineering of R. toruloides for producing value-added compounds and provide a valuable reference for the genetic manipulation of other oleaginous basidiomycetous yeasts.

title: Inhibition of WNT signaling sensitizes CRC cells to anti-tumor effects of retinoids: basis for new drug combinations in oncology.
authors: Hunsu VO, Facey COB, Opdenaker LM, Boman BM
abstract: Our Goal is to sensitize human colorectal cancer (CRC) to the differentiation-inducing effects of retinoic acid (RA) agents by suppressing WNT signaling. Previously, we reported that the WNT and RA pathways are functionally linked, and in CRC, APC mutation generates a WNT:RA imbalance leading to incomplete differentiation and stem cell (SC) overpopulation. Hypothesis: Therapeutically inhibiting WNT signaling enhances the ability of retinoid agents to induce growth suppression and differentiation. We tested drug combinations of: (1) anti-WNT agents (Sulindac & Piroxicam) that produce anti-tumor activity in humans and animals harboring germline APC mutations, with (2) RA agents (All-trans-RA, 9-cis RA) and RA metabolism blocking agent (CYP26A1 inhibitors Liarozole and Talarozole), which inhibit proliferation and induce differentiation of CRC cell lines. Results: The combined effect of anti-WNT agents and RA drugs shows additive or synergistic responses in CRC cell lines compared to single agents. Drug combinations decrease the proportion of aldehyde dehydrogenase-positive SCs and increase neuroendocrine cell differentiation in CRC cells that show a synergistic response to treatment. NanoString profiling shows that therapeutically decreasing WNT signaling in CRC cells significantly changes the effect of RA signaling on gene expression. Treating human CRC organoid cultures and PDX mouse models with WNT:RA-based drug combinations led to greater anti-tumor activity as compared to individual agents. Conclusion: Inhibiting WNT signaling effectively sensitizes CRC cells to the anti-tumor effects of retinoids. These findings have important clinical significance for designing new drug combinations against CRC.

title: Akkermansia muciniphila protects diabetes-associated cognitive decline by enhancing leucine catabolism and suppressing neuronal excessive mitophagy.
authors: Ye X, Cai Q, Li Y, You M, Chen J, Pan Y, Zhu M, Lu Z
abstract: Dysregulation of the gut-brain metabolic axis has been implicated in the progression of diabetes-associated cognitive decline (DACD), yet its underlying mechanism remains largely unknown. Herein, we identified a low abundance of Akkermansia muciniphila (AKK) and high leucine levels as key driving factors of DACD in both diabetic mice and patients. Our results revealed that AKK bacteria hold the capacity to catabolize leucine, and the elevated leucine levels observed in diabetic mice and patients are partly attributed to a low abundance of AKK bacteria. Moreover, leucine supplementation and deprivation further confirmed that excessive leucine accelerated and aggravated the progression of DACD in mice. Mechanistically, leucine directly modulated the phosphorylation of TBK1 and, in turn, phosphorylated the autophagy adaptor OPTN, thereby enhancing its binding capacity to LC3 and Ub chains and triggering neuronal excessive mitophagy. Therefore, this study uncovers a new mechanism of the gut-brain metabolic axis involved in DACD progression and provides a novel perspective for gut-targeted therapy of cognitive disorders.

title: Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
authors: Braatz E, Stenman M, Al-Mousli J, Dalén M, Olsson C
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp (n = 261) or MHCA (n = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, p = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank p = 0.33). CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.

title: Feasibility and potential benefits of daily online adaptive radiotherapy for head and neck cancer without margin reduction using an RTT-only workflow.
authors: Lindegaard AM, Håkansson K, Appelt A, Bernsdorf M, Gothelf AB, Jensen TRB, Mohammad A, Kristensen CA
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Online adaptive radiotherapy (oART) may improve head and neck cancer (HNC) treatment, where anatomical changes during radiotherapy (RT) are common. However, oART is resource-intensive and clinical data are limited. We conducted a prospective feasibility trial implementating an RT technologist (RTT)-led workflow to evaluate dosimetric outcomes, workflow strategies, and intrafractional motion in daily oART. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Ten patients receiving curatively intended oART (33-34 fractions) using standard PTV margins were included (NCT: 07506902). For each fraction, a scheduled plan (original plan recalculated on daily anatomy) and an adapted plan (reoptimized to daily anatomy) were generated, and the preferred plan was delivered. Target coverage (PTV1 V95%), mean dose (Dmean) and maximum dose (Dmax) to selected organs at risk (OAR), treatment time, and baseline target volume were extracted for all fractions. The effect of oART (scheduled- versus delivered plan) was analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Intrafractional motion was assessed weekly. RESULTS: A total of 322 adaptive session were completed. The median treatment time was 29.9 min. The adapted plan was selected in 78% of fractions. oART improved target coverage in 76% of fractions. Dmean decreased for the oral cavity (-2.4 Gy, p < 0.001) but increased for the middle PCM (2.5 Gy, p < 0.001). Dmax increased for the brainstem (2.9 Gy, p < 0.001) and spinal cord (2.2 Gy, p < 0.001). Intrafractional motion was within PTV margins, with few patient-specific exceedances. CONCLUSION: Daily oART for HNC is feasible with improvements in target coverage but modest and inconsistent OAR sparing.

title: Cortex-grounded diffusion models for brain image generation.
authors: Bongratz F, Li Y, Elbaroudy S, Grimmer T, Yakushev I, Hedderich DM, Wachinger C
abstract: Synthetic neuroimaging data can mitigate critical limitations of real-world datasets, including the scarcity of rare phenotypes, domain shifts across scanners, and insufficient longitudinal coverage. However, existing generative models largely rely on weak conditioning signals, such as labels or text, which lack anatomical grounding and often produce biologically implausible outputs. To this end, we introduce Cor2Vox, a cortex-grounded generative framework for brain magnetic resonance image (MRI) synthesis that ties image generation to continuous structural priors of the cerebral cortex. It leverages high-resolution cortical surfaces to guide a 3D shape-to-image Brownian bridge diffusion process, enabling topologically faithful synthesis and precise control over underlying anatomies. To support the generation of new, realistic brain shapes, we developed a large-scale statistical shape model of cortical morphology derived from over 33,000 UK Biobank scans. We validated the fidelity of Cor2Vox based on traditional image quality metrics, advanced cortical surface reconstruction, and whole-brain segmentation quality, outperforming many baseline methods. Across three applications, namely (i) anatomy-guided synthesis, (ii) simulation of progressive gray matter atrophy, and (iii) harmonization of in-house frontotemporal dementia scans with public datasets, Cor2Vox preserved fine-grained cortical morphology at the sub-voxel level. Notably, the proposed model exhibits inherent robustness to variations in cortical geometry and unseen dementia phenotypes without retraining, paving the way for disease progression modeling and robust data augmentation in rare neurodegenerative disorders.

title: MSRepaint: Multiple Sclerosis Repaint with conditional denoising diffusion implicit model for bidirectional lesion filling and synthesis.
authors: Zhang J, Zuo L, Liu Y, Zhang H, Remedios SW, Landman BA, Calabresi PA, Saidha S
abstract: In multiple sclerosis (MS), lesions interfere with automated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) analyses such as brain parcellation and deformable registration, while lesion segmentation models are hindered by the limited availability of annotated training data. To address both issues, we propose MSRepaint, a unified diffusion-based generative model for bidirectional lesion filling and synthesis that restores anatomical continuity for downstream analyses and augments segmentation through realistic data generation. MSRepaint conditions on spatial lesion masks for voxel-level control, incorporates contrast dropout to handle missing inputs, integrates a repainting mechanism to preserve surrounding anatomy during lesion filling and synthesis, and employs a multi-view DDIM inversion and fusion pipeline for 3D consistency with fast inference. Extensive evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of MSRepaint across multiple tasks. For lesion filling, we evaluate both the accuracy within the filled regions and the impact on downstream tasks including brain parcellation and deformable registration. MSRepaint outperforms the FSL and NiftySeg lesion filling methods, and achieves accuracy on par with FastSurfer-LIT, a recent diffusion model-based lesion filling method, while offering over 20×faster inference. For lesion synthesis, state-of-the-art MS lesion segmentation models trained on MSRepaint-synthesized data outperform those trained on CarveMix-synthesized data or real ISBI challenge training data across multiple benchmarks, including the MICCAI 2016 and UMCL datasets. Additionally, we demonstrate that MSRepaint's unified bidirectional filling and synthesis capability, with full spatial control over lesion appearance, enables high-fidelity mask-conditioned voxel-wise control of lesion appearance within a unified framework. Our code is available at https://github.com/Jinwei1209/msrepaint.

title: Anatomy-informed multi-task framework for visceral artery aneurysm screening on non-contrast CT.
authors: Xu Z, Liu T, Bai L, Wang H, Zhang J, Wang Z, Li H, Hu Y
abstract: Visceral artery aneurysm (VAA) screening on non-contrast CT (NCCT) is fundamentally a structure-constrained representation learning problem under weak vascular contrast. In NCCT, visceral arteries lack explicit lumen enhancement, and aneurysms often appear only as subtle local dilatations embedded in thin and branching vascular structures. This makes conventional intensity-driven segmentation unreliable and demands models that can preserve vascular continuity, capture subtle lesion morphology, and leverage anatomical context at the same time. To address this problem, we propose an anatomy-informed multi-task framework for NCCT-based VAA screening. Built on a Mamba-based segmentation backbone, our method reshapes token propagation according to vascular structure, enabling anatomy-consistent long-range dependency modeling without changing the original state space dynamics. To further strengthen the learned representation, we incorporate hierarchical anatomical supervision through global vessel-location classification and local patch-wise lesion prediction, so that the embedding is guided by both coarse anatomical semantics and fine-grained lesion evidence. We further introduce a prototype-based inference strategy that uses feature-space similarity to suppress morphologically confusing false positives. Extensive experiments on internal and external cohorts show that the proposed framework improves lesion segmentation, reduces false positives, and generalizes robustly across multiple cohorts. These results demonstrate that geometry-aware and anatomy-informed representation learning provides an effective and practical solution for VAA opportunistic screening on NCCT.

title: Trait-like proteomic signatures of stress resilience: correlates of freeze-like response resistance.
authors: Kučera J, Makarová M, Vít M, Novák J, Zlámal F, Ráčková L, Fialová Kučerová J, Grulichová M
abstract: The freeze-like response is a fundamental defensive mechanism that remains poorly understood despite its potential to impair functioning under acute threat. We examined its biological correlates using untargeted serum proteomics in participants exposed to ecologically valid simulated armed attacks, comparing untrained individuals (n = 20) with experienced police rapid response personnel (n = 20). Freeze-like responses, characterized by unresponsiveness to attack, were assessed via expert video analysis of participant performance during the scenarios. Serum samples collected before and after threat exposure were analyzed via LC‒MS/MS, identifying 1,238 protein groups. Experienced personnel demonstrated markedly greater resistance to freeze-like responses. No significant proteomic changes were observed from pre- to post-exposure in either group, suggesting that freeze-resistance may be associated with stable, trait-like signatures rather than acute stress-responsive processes. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified a module strongly correlated with freeze-resistance (r = 0.75, p = 4 × 10-9) and training status (r = 0.71, p = 6 × 10-8), which also correlated with skeletal muscle mass (r = 0.57, p = 8 × 10-5). This module was enriched for processes including extracellular matrix organization, muscle development, carbohydrate metabolism, and antioxidant activity. These molecular patterns may reflect the downstream effects of comprehensive training that integrates physical conditioning, operational experience, and psychological preparation. This study provides the first proteomic characterization of freeze-like response resistance under realistic threat conditions, supporting the view that resilience involves stable physiological adaptations rather than solely reactive stress mechanisms.

title: Isolation and characterization of rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes: Establishing a foundation for studies of intramuscular fat metabolism.
authors: Ahamba IS, Song G, Kinkpe L, Duan Q, Goswami N, Jin Z, Wu J, Dong X
abstract: Intramuscular fat (IMF) significantly influences meat quality, affecting flavor, tenderness, and juiciness. Despite extensive research on livestock such as cattle and pigs, the regulation of IMF in rabbits remains poorly understood. This study establishes a standardized in vitro method for isolating and characterizing intramuscular preadipocytes from the longissimus dorsi muscle of 3-day-old Hycole rabbits using enzymatic digestion and differential centrifugation. Three-day-old neonates were selected for initial protocol development due to their higher progenitor cell abundance and tissue accessibility, which facilitates method optimization and ensures consistent cell yields. Isolated cells displayed typical preadipocyte morphology and expressed key markers, including PREF-1, PPARγ, and Leptin, confirmed by RT-qPCR and immunofluorescence. Upon adipogenic induction, cells exhibited progressive lipid accumulation, as indicated by Oil Red O staining, and showed upregulated expression of PPARG, C/EBPa, and FABP4, confirming their differentiation potential. This study establishes a comprehensive protocol for isolating rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes, providing a foundational tool for investigating the molecular mechanisms of adipogenesis in lagomorphs. The model supports future studies on genetic and nutritional strategies to enhance rabbit meat quality while preserving its lean characteristics.

title: Oxygen-vacancy-rich LDH sonosensitizers potentiate narrow-spectrum antibiotics via membrane-disruption strategy for mixed bacterial wound infections.
authors: Xi L, Liu X, Yu C, Wang T, Liao J, Lv Y, Zhang M, Zhang Y
abstract: Mixed bacterial infections, including Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogens, remain a major global health concern. Achieving efficient treatment of synergistic polymicrobial infections stills a tremendous clinical challenge due to antibiotic permeability barriers and resistance. Here, we construct a defect-engineered layered double hydroxide (LDH)-based sonosensitizer platform loaded with clindamycin (a-CoW/CLD) for mixed bacterial infection therapy, which not only demonstrates high efficacy against Gram-positive bacteria, but also exploits reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated membrane disruption of Gram-negative bacteria to facilitate CLD penetration, thereby achieving broad-spectrum and highly efficient killing of mixed bacteria. The amorphous a-CoW nanosheets, enriched with oxygen vacancies via acid etching, exhibit a substantially narrowed bandgap (1.22 eV) and markedly enhanced charge separation, producing 22.1-fold higher singlet oxygen under ultrasound (US) irradiation compared with pristine CoW. This ROS burst synergized with CLD achieves potent killing of Staphylococcus aureus (>99.9% at 20 μg mL-1). More critically, ROS disrupt the outer membrane of Gram-negative Escherichia coli, promoting CLD internalization and consequently boosting its lethality by 18.4-fold (from ∼5% to >92.1%). Mechanistic transcriptomics reveals ROS and CLD synergy: ROS disrupt the bacterial membrane via lipid peroxidation, enabling CLD penetration to block protein synthesis and metabolism, while ROS also induce oxidative stress, collectively leading to bacterial death. In a murine wound model co-infected with both pathogens, a-CoW/CLD plus US eradicates >99.9% of mixed bacteria, suppresses systemic inflammation, and significantly accelerates angiogenesis and re-epithelialization. This paradigm establishes a low-dose, broad-spectrum sonodynamic-antibiotic strategy that overcomes antibiotic permeability bottleneck, offering a promising therapeutic avenue against mixed bacterial infections.

title: Guanidine-quaternary ammonium polymer-derived carbon dots differentially modulate bacterial respiration and osteoblast mitochondria to resolve infection and foster osteointegration.
authors: Bai X, Qin A, Wang Z, Kong G, Zhang M, Li H, Zhao R, Yu Y
abstract: Implant-associated infections (IAIs) represent one of the most challenging complications following orthopedic implantation. Current antibacterial strategies struggle to achieve complete pathogen eradication while maintaining sustained osteogenic activity at the implant-bone interface. Leveraging the spatial divergence in energy metabolism between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, we designed and synthesized guanidine-quaternary ammonium polymer-derived carbon dots (GQCDs) with confirmed structure. Under non-infected conditions, GQCDs enhance mitochondrial metabolism to promote bone regeneration. In infected microenvironments, GQCDs not only selectively target bacterial membranes and inhibit the respiratory chain to exert potent antibacterial effects, but also downregulate host inflammatory responses and restore mitochondrial function in osteoblasts, thereby creating a favorable microenvironment for bone repair. GQCDs can be stably integrated onto various clinical implant substrates via a coating process. GQCDs-coated implants possessed the dual antibacterial and osteogenic functionalities, which were validated using in vitro co-culture systems and in vivo implant infection models in rats and beagles, offering a promising strategy with encouraging translational prospects to address IAIs.

title: Microbial succession and genome-resolved metabolic functions shape flavor evolution during sauce-flavor Baijiu fermentation.
authors: Niu J, Li W, Chen X, Zhu H, Sun W, Li X, Sun B
abstract: Sauce-flavor Baijiu (SFB) fermentation is characterized by a unique multi-round solid-state process, during which complex microbial succession drives flavor formation. However, the functional differentiation and metabolic mechanisms of microbial communities across successive fermentation rounds remain poorly understood. In this study, the physicochemical properties, microbial assembly, and metabolic profiles of fermented grains (FG) were investigated across seven production rounds (R1-R7). The results revealed that as fermentation rounds progressed, the FG environment evolved toward elevated acidity and reduced pH, driving a directional shift in the microbial community from an initially diverse assemblage to a structure dominated by acid-tolerant Acetilactobacillus, which established pronounced ecological dominance in later rounds. Metabolomic analysis further indicated that this dynamic adjustment of microbial structure drove the evolution of the flavor profile, specifically manifesting as differential accumulation of compounds such as esters, alcohols, and pyrazines across the various rounds. Co-occurrence network analysis demonstrated that positive microbial interactions significantly predominated within the fermentation system, and that community function exhibited a convergent trend as the rounds increased. Furthermore, 158 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) were recovered, and metabolic reconstruction elucidated the potential contributions of genera such as Pediococcus, Bacillus, and Oceanobacillus to key metabolic pathways, including glycolysis, phenylalanine metabolism, and pyrazine biosynthesis. This work provides important insights into microbial regulation and quality improvement in SFB fermentation.

title: Interpreting glycine-associated phenotypes in Lactiplantibacillus plantarum: the need for strain-specific and medium-controlled evidence.
authors: Li J, Zhang X
abstract: Han et al. report that glycine supplementation alters growth-associated readouts and improves bile and osmotic stress tolerance in Lactiplantibacillus plantarum KCCM 11322. We agree that these phenotypes may be relevant to starter-culture optimization, but the mechanistic attribution to metabolic remodeling remains incomplete. Pathway inference was based on a reference L. plantarum annotation rather than the KCCM 11322 genome; experiments used chemically undefined MRS, so 0 mM denotes no added glycine rather than a glycine-free baseline; and pH was not systematically controlled. The divergence between visible biomass, OD600, and CFU at high glycine concentrations further emphasizes the need to separate biomass accumulation from viable growth. Strain-specific genomics, defined-medium experiments, pH-matched controls, and targeted metabolic measurements would clarify whether glycine acts as a nutrient, physicochemical modifier, or regulator of metabolic flux.

title: Functional genomic insights into aac(6')-I-associated kanamycin resistance in Leuconostoc citreum DMLC16.
authors: Lee S, Heo S, Moon Y, Kim M, Jeong DW
abstract: Leuconostoc (L.) citreum strain DMLC16 was initially selected as a candidate starter culture for fermented foods. However, it exhibited a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 256 mg/L against kanamycin, exceeding the European Food Safety Authority threshold for resistance. To determine whether this resistance was intrinsic or acquired, comparative genomic analysis was performed with four additional L. citreum strains. Only DMLC16 was found to harbor the aminoglycoside 6'-N-acetyltransferase (aac(6')-I) gene. An adjacent IS30 family transposase and a putative recognition sequence (5'-TGTTGAGTACAGGTTG-3') were also identified, and the surrounding chromosomal region contained a replication initiation protein typically associated with plasmids, strongly suggesting that aac(6')-I represents an acquired trait. Functional validation confirmed its role in resistance: cloning of aac(6')-I conferred increased kanamycin MICs in Gram-positive hosts, rising from 4 to 64 mg/L in Staphylococcus aureus RN4220 and from 2 to 32 mg/L in Lactococcuscremoris MG1363. These findings indicate that L. citreum DMLC16 carries an acquired genetic determinant conferring kanamycin resistance. In contrast, species-level comparative genomic analysis suggested that conserved sequence variations in the 16S rRNA gene and gidB may contribute to the intrinsic kanamycin resistance phenotype of L. citreum. These observations highlight the need for strain-level genomic screening to identify acquired resistance determinants, together with further investigation of species-wide kanamycin susceptibility patterns and the genetic basis of intrinsic resistance. Importantly, L. citreum strains harboring aac(6')-I should not be considered suitable candidates for industrial starter cultures.

title: A modular in vitro multienzyme cascade for the sustainable synthesis of high-value vidarabine 5'-monophosphate from adenosine.
authors: Su W, Zhang X, Li R, Li K, Guo X, Liu X, Wang Z, Wang H
abstract: Nucleoside analogues such as vidarabine (Ara-A) are vital therapeutics but are often limited by poor pharmacokinetics. Its phosphorylated form, vidarabine 5'-monophosphate (Ara-AMP), offers improved solubility and is used as a clinical alternative, although it can be dephosphorylated to Ara-A in vivo. Here, we report a modular multienzyme cascade for the sustainable synthesis of Ara-AMP directly from adenosine. The cascade integrates three functional modules: a core module (PNP, PPM, and RpiA) for the conversion of adenosine to Ara-A, a driver module (dNKδ20) for the selective phosphorylation of Ara-A to Ara-AMP, and a support module (PPK) for ATP regeneration from low-cost ADP and polyphosphate. The use of dNKδ20, a mutant deoxyribonucleoside kinase with high selectivity for Ara-A over adenosine, is critical for minimizing the formation of AMP byproduct, which would otherwise complicate downstream processing. Under optimized conditions, the cascade achieved an 80.2% conversion of 1 mM adenosine to Ara-AMP in 4 h using 0.05 mM ADP. The modular design was also applicable to guanosine and inosine, affording the corresponding arabinosyl nucleotides, albeit with lower yields. This work establishes a sustainable biocatalytic platform for nucleoside analogues, exemplifying how enzyme promiscuity, thermodynamic driving, and cofactor recycling enable green pharmaceutical manufacturing.

title: Reprogramming NOX4-associated ferro-aging with an iron-chelating senescent-cell-targeted therapy for intervertebral disc degeneration.
authors: Wang J, Chen Q, Xing J, Sun Y, Yan C, Zhao B, Han L, Sun J
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) has been a major contributor to chronic low back pain, yet effective disease-modifying therapies remain limited. Here, we identified a NOX4-associated ferro-aging program linking iron overload, oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and cellular senescence in degenerative NPCs. Clinical imaging, transcriptomic analyses, human disc specimens, iron-overloaded NPCs, and naturally aged rats consistently revealed ferro-aging-associated changes during IVDD. Mechanistically, gain- and loss-of-function, genetic rescue, and temporal analyses positioned NOX4 as an upstream oxidative regulator of ROS-dependent ACSL4 activation, lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and NPC senescence. Natural-product screening identified amentoflavone (Amen) as a candidate NOX4-interacting compound that suppresses membrane-associated NADPH oxidase activity in a NOX4-dependent manner. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses showed that ferro-aging NPCs exhibited increased NKG2D ligand-related stress signals, reduced endocytic activity, and enhanced membrane-fusion features. Guided by these characteristics, we engineered SenoFAN, an Amen-loaded, iron-chelating phenolic nanozyme coated with NKG2D-engineered NPC membranes. SenoFAN integrates iron sequestration, nanozyme-mediated redox remodeling, Amen-mediated NOX4-dependent suppression of NADPH oxidase activity, and ferro-aging-cell-adapted delivery through NKG2D-ligand recognition and membrane fusion. In vitro, SenoFAN reduced labile iron and oxidative stress, restored mitochondrial and lipid homeostasis, and suppressed lipid peroxidation and senescence. In a rat puncture-induced IVDD model, SenoFAN showed preferential association with ferro-aging-associated NPCs, prolonged intradiscal retention, reduced iron deposition and senescence, preserved disc structure, and showed favorable biosafety. Collectively, our findings identify NOX4-associated ferro-aging as a therapeutically actionable pathological program in IVDD, while establishing an upstream regulatory role for NOX4 in the FAC-induced ferro-aging model.

title: Discovery and characterization of potent and efficacious small-molecule parathyroid hormone Receptor-1 (PTH1R) antagonists for the treatment of hypercalcemia.
authors: Pontillo J, Wang S, Zhu Y, Rico-Bautista E, Shintaku J, Urgaonkar S, Antwan A, Betz SF
abstract: Primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) is caused by the enlargement and overactivation of one or more of the parathyroid glands, via parathyroid adenomas or hyperplasia. This results in over-secretion of PTH hormone, which results in agonism of PTH1R and subsequent hypercalcemia. Blocking PTH action via an oral, small-molecule PTH1R antagonist may provide a convenient and improved therapy for PHPT. Herein, we report the discovery, optimization and characterization of a highly potent, bioavailable and efficacious series represented by 9c (hPTH1R IC50 = 5.2 nM), which based on pharmacokinetics and biological activity, represents a significant preclinical advancement in the development of small-molecule PTH antagonists.

title: Targeting tumor-selective membrane-associated PCNA enables selective antibody-drug conjugate therapy.
authors: Abu Ahmad M, Ungar-Malma NM, Naumchik A, Machluf-Katz N, Radinsky O, Adi Eisdorfer S, Gara A, Istoyler Y
abstract: Membrane-associated proliferating cell nuclear antigen (mPCNA) is an attractive tumor-selective antigen for antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) development. We generated a chimeric IgG1 ADC, RC14-MMAE, to exploit three key properties of mPCNA that support its use as an efficient delivery platform. First, flow-cytometric and imaging analyses show abundant mPCNA surface expression on multiple tumor cell lines and in JIMT1 xenografts, providing accessible epitopes for binding. Second, comparative profiling against non-malignant counterparts and normal mouse tissues reveals minimal or undetectable mPCNA at the plasma membrane of healthy cells, indicating a sharp tumor-normal differential expected to limit off-tumor targeting and improve the therapeutic window. Third, live-cell internalization assays demonstrate that RC14 rapidly accumulates in LAMP1-positive lysosomes after engaging mPCNA, confirming efficient trafficking along the endolysosomal pathway required for protease-mediated cleavage of the valine-citrulline linker and release of monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE). Consistent with this target profile, RC14-MMAE exhibits potent antigen-dependent cytotoxicity in mPCNA-positive tumor models in NSG mice, favorable pharmacokinetics, sustained payload retention in serum, robust in vivo antitumor activity with limited overt toxicity, and a significantly increased fraction of F4/80⁺ tumor-infiltrating myeloid cells within dissociated tumors. These findings establish mPCNA as a functionally validated, tumor-selective internalizing target and support RC14-MMAE as a first-in-class mPCNA-directed ADC with broad translational potential.

title: Sensitive detection of 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal-modified proteins in oxidative stress-related diseases.
authors: Méndez-Cuadro D, Kamali AN, Ruiz C, Pérez-Benavente S, Hernáez ML, Rodríguez-Cavallo E, Puyet A, Bautista JM
abstract: Protein modification by 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal (HNE) is associated with metabolic, neurodegenerative, and infectious diseases characterized by oxidative stress. Detecting low-abundance HNE-protein adducts in complex extracts requires antibodies with suitable reactivity and selectivity. We generated polyclonal antisera in rabbits using matched-species rabbit serum albumin modified in vitro with HNE (RSA-HNE), administered either intact or after tryptic digestion. The antisera displayed distinct recognition profiles across dot blot, ELISA, and Western blot assays using HNE-modified standards and membrane-protein extracts from uninfected and Plasmodium falciparum-infected human erythrocytes. Antiserum 1, raised against intact RSA-HNE, showed the stronger overall immunochemical response, whereas Antiserum 2, raised against tryptic RSA-HNE, displayed a different and more restricted peptide-recognition profile. In an immunoenrichment and LC-MS/MS workflow, Antiserum 1 recovered 14 candidate HNE-associated membrane proteins from erythrocytes infected with P. falciparum trophozoites. Site-specific evidence remained tentative for four peptides. These antisera are therefore proposed as research tools for studying protein lipoxidation, although biological replication and orthogonal validation of the candidate modification sites are required.

title: CATH-1 supplementation improves sperm quality and fertility of rooster semen during cold storage by reducing bacterial contamination.
authors: Authaida S, Boonkum W, Duangjinda M, Shimada M, Kaeoket K, Rerkyusuke S, Chankitisakul V
abstract: The present study investigated the effects of antibiotic and antimicrobial peptide supplementation on semen quality, viable bacterial load, and fertility potential in Thai native chickens during cold storage. Semen samples were diluted in an extender supplemented with kanamycin (31.20 μg/mL) or CATH-1 (3.75 or 7.50 μg/mL) and stored at 5 °C for up to 72 h. Sperm quality parameters, viable bacterial load, and reproductive outcomes following artificial insemination were assessed at 0, 24, 48, and 72 h. Storage duration significantly affected all sperm quality parameters (P < 0.001), while fertility and hatchability were progressively lower across the sequential storage-time phases. Kanamycin and CATH-1 at 3.75 μg/mL consistently maintained higher sperm quality and reduced susceptibility to lipid peroxidation compared with the control (P < 0.05), with no significant difference between the two treatments. Both treatments effectively suppressed bacterial proliferation; however, viable bacterial load increased progressively beyond 24 h in all groups. Scanning electron microscopy revealed marked bacterial surface alterations following CATH-1 treatment, consistent with membrane-disruptive antibacterial activity. In contrast, CATH-1 at 7.50 μg/mL compromised sperm quality and reproductive outcomes from the initial time point onward, despite achieving the greatest bacterial suppression among all treatments. Across the sequential storage-time phases, fertility potential was progressively lower, although the kanamycin and CATH-1 (3.75 μg/mL) groups maintained higher fertility than the control during prolonged storage. These findings demonstrate a dose-dependent dual effect of CATH-1, with 3.75 μg/mL performing comparably to kanamycin and representing a promising antibiotic alternative in the context of One Health concerns in poultry artificial insemination programs.

title: Implementing a First Nation data-sovereign and agile modelling platform for pandemic management: lessons from Manitoba.
authors: Phillips-Beck W, Lavoie JG, Star L, Nickel N, Romanescu R
abstract: This paper describes lessons learned from a partnership between the First Nations Health and Social Secretariat of Manitoba (FNHSSM) and researchers at the University of Manitoba to develop a community-led COVID-19 modelling platform. The envisioned tool would allow First Nations leaders to input local data and generate outputs to support decision-making using a stochastic, age-stratified agent-based model of COVID-19 transmission. Although the platform was not fully operationalized during the project, several important lessons emerged. First, the COVID-19 pandemic placed significant demands on human resources, making such an ambitious initiative difficult to implement during an active public health emergency. Second, the project required coordination among multiple teams with distinct expertise, including model developers, dashboard designers, and FNHSSM information technology staff responsible for infrastructure planning. Competing pandemic-related priorities frequently delayed collaboration and implementation. Third, access to administrative data through the Manitoba Centre for Health Policy involved a six-month reporting lag, limiting the availability of timely information needed for emergency response and decision-making. These challenges highlight structural barriers to data-driven pandemic management in First Nations communities. We recommend: (1) providing First Nations organizations and communities with ongoing access to their own administrative data for service delivery, planning, and emergency management; and (2) establishing First Nations-led data centres with sustainable infrastructure and core funding to support data sovereignty, agile reporting, and future public health response efforts.
